subject: Clarify pricing & batching assumptions — follow-up from demo
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@fintechco.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify pricing & batching assumptions — follow-up from demo

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — Tom and I appreciated the throughput examples and the batching tradeoffs you walked through. A couple of quick items we wanted to confirm before we move this to procurement:

- Volumes: rough estimate is 250M tokens/month to start, scaling to ~1B tokens/month in 12 months. We can provide tighter numbers but wanted a working assumption.
- Target unit economics: our CFO asked us to aim for ~$800–1,200 per 1M tokens for inference (including token generation + embedding calls). Is that achievable with your Dedicated or Hosted tiers?
- Batching & concurrency: our workload is a mix of interactive chat (50% of traffic, P95 latency < 400ms desired) and background scoring (50%, throughput-focused). For chat we expect many short sessions with continuous small bursts; for scoring we expect long sequences and high concurrency. Curious what continuous batching assumptions you typically make and any recommended concurrency settings.

Can you sketch a short, pragmatic set of assumptions we can use in our eRFP? Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up if helpful.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Li
Head of ML Platforms | FintechCo
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@fintechco.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@fintechco.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify pricing & batching assumptions — follow-up from demo

Sarah — great to connect earlier, and thanks for the clear bullets. I pulled together a concise recap and a baseline estimate attached (redwood-pricing-estimate.pdf) so your finance/procurement team has something to react to. Key points below and a couple of clarifying questions.

Recap / baseline assumptions (hosted & dedicated comparatives):
- Start volume: 250M tokens/mo (month 1) -> 1B tokens/mo (month 12)
- Baseline target: we can target $900–1,100 per 1M tokens on Dedicated with conservative batching; Hosted can be slightly higher depending on burst profile.
- Batching model: we assume continuous batching with auto-batching windows tuned to keep P95 chat latency <400ms for 99% sessions; scoring jobs will be routed to higher-batch, lower-cost lanes.
- Concurrency guidance: for interactive chat expect an average concurrency per worker of 8–16 short-lived sessions; for scoring consider dedicated pools with concurrency 32–64 depending on sequence length.

Questions we need from you to tighten the estimate:
1) Average tokens per chat session (prompt + response) — ballpark (e.g., 150–400)?
2) Sequence length distribution for scoring jobs (median and P95) and whether they can be batched across requests.
3) SLA preference: is Hosted API OK with 99.5% availability, or do you need Dedicated + SLA?

Attachments: redwood-pricing-estimate.pdf (PDF, 48 KB) — includes a worked example showing per-1M token costs under different batching/concurrency profiles.

Next steps:
- If you can send answers to 1–3 above, we will produce a two-slide summary and a one-page procurement-ready cost table (Hosted vs Dedicated).
- Optional: 30-min technical deep-dive with David (solutions architect) to review batching knobs and caching (I copied him).

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Tue 03/24 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 03/25 09:00–09:30 PT. Which works best?

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-pricing-estimate.pdf (48 KB)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 18:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify pricing & batching assumptions — internal note

Aisha — quick internal note before we finalize the external follow-up:

- If FintechCo's chat sessions are ~200 tokens/session average, the continuous batching approach with prefix/KV caching will likely get us to the lower end (~$850/1M) on Dedicated for stable traffic.
- For scoring with long sequences (>=1024 tokens), we should recommend a quantized model variant and a high-batch lane; cost drops substantially per token but latency rises — call that out for their SREs.
- Concurrency: interactive pool should target 10–12 average concurrency per worker, with autoscale burst to 40 for sudden surges. Use circuit-breaker policy to fall back to a medium-cost variant if tail queues grow.

I'll draft the technical slide David mentioned and drop into the deck. Keep the ask light externally until we get the session length distribution.

-David
David Kim
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@fintechco.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@fintechco.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify pricing & batching assumptions — follow-up and proposal

Sarah / Tom — thanks for the quick response on the call. Per David's internal guidance (copied above), here is a concise, procurement-ready summary and proposed next steps. I attached a short requirements workbook so your infra team can drop numbers in.

Baseline cost guidance (conservative):
- Start (250M tokens/mo): $1,000 per 1M tokens (Hosted baseline) — estimate row in attached workbook.
- Dedicated (committed, month-to-month smoothing): $900 per 1M tokens with continuous batching and caching; can approach $800/1M with 12-month commit + higher batch lanes for scoring.

Batching & concurrency assumptions we used in the numbers:
- Chat (interactive): average session 200 tokens, continuous batching window ~15–25ms, target P95 latency <400ms. Per-worker concurrency 10–12 average; autoscale to 40 for spikes.
- Scoring (batchable): typical sequence median 512 tokens, P95 1,200 tokens. Use dedicated high-batch pools (batch size target 32–128 depending on sequence length) with concurrency 32–64.
- Caching: prefix and KV cache estimated to save ~12–18% token compute for repeated prompts (we applied a 10% conservative reduction in the cost model).

Action items / next steps:
1) Please complete the attached FintechCo_ML_Reqs.xlsx (tab: workload_inputs) with: monthly token volumes by month, average tokens per chat session, scoring sequence distribution (median/P95), and SLA preference.
2) We will convert your inputs into a procurement table (Hosted vs Dedicated) + a 1-page SOW-level note on rollout and fallback policies.
3) Book the technical deep-dive if you want us to walk through batching knobs (we're good Tue 03/24 10:00 PT or Wed 03/25 09:00 PT).

Attachments: FintechCo_ML_Reqs.xlsx (Excel, 12 KB)

If you prefer I can also push a stripped-down one-page price schedule to DocuSign once volumes are locked.

Cheers,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
